what_it_is.prose: Astra Microwave Products Limited (AMPL) is a Hyderabad-based, BSE/NSE-listed (532493 / ASTRAMICRO) RF and microwave subsystems champion founded in 1991. The company is a critical supplier to India's defence electronics ecosystem, providing RF/microwave components, subsystems, and radars for the Akash SAM, BrahMos, Tejas, and naval programmes. Astra's flagship recent contract is the ₹2,205.23 crore HAL order signed on 30 July 2026 for the Uttam AESA radar programme — 122 Active Antenna Array Units and 121 Interface Frames for the Tejas Mk-1A/Mk-2. This contract drove Astra's order book to a record ₹4,300 crore as of August 2026 (up from ₹1,916 crore standalone / ₹2,209 crore consolidated at end-Q2 FY26). FY26 consolidated revenue was ₹1,163 crore (+11% YoY), with FY26 inflows of ₹1,660 crore (+29% YoY). Management is targeting 15% FY27 revenue growth to approximately ₹1,350 crore, with a 6-7x long-term revenue opportunity cited. In counter-UAS, Astra launched the 'Drishti Counter UAV Radar' (4 km range for 0.001 sq m targets, 100+ simultaneous drone tracks) at Aero India 2023 in February 2023, alongside a complete C-UAS System combining active radar, passive RF sensors, and multi-band jamming. Astra was one of four vendors (alongside L&T, Adani Defence, and ECIL) to receive DRDO's Counter-Drone System Transfer of Technology in April 2022. Astra also operates a joint venture with Rafael Comsys Private Limited, which received a ₹255.88 crore MoD order on 13 December 2024. Astra has announced a space arm demerger (timeline TBD).

faq.question: What is Astra Microwave's role in the Tejas programme?
faq.answer: Astra Microwave is a critical supplier to the HAL Tejas programme. On 30 July 2026, Astra signed a ₹2,205.23 crore contract with HAL for 122 Active Antenna Array Units and 121 Interface Frames for the indigenous Uttam AESA radar — the primary radar for the Tejas Mk-1A and Mk-2. This contract drove Astra's order book to a record ₹4,300 crore by August 2026. The Uttam AESA radar is DRDO-designed, with Astra supplying the active antenna array sub-assemblies.

faq.question: Does Astra Microwave make counter-drone systems?
faq.answer: Yes. Astra launched the 'Drishti Counter UAV Radar' (4 km range for 0.001 sq m targets, 100+ simultaneous drone tracks) at Aero India 2023 in February 2023, alongside a complete C-UAS System combining active radar, passive RF sensors, and multi-band jamming. Astra was one of four vendors (alongside L&T, Adani Defence, and ECIL) to receive DRDO's Counter-Drone System Transfer of Technology in April 2022. The Drishti C-UAS is a modest part of Astra's overall business; the company is primarily an RF/microwave subsystems supplier.

faq.question: What is Astra Microwave's financial performance?
faq.answer: FY26 consolidated revenue was ₹1,163 crore (+11% YoY), with Q4 FY26 PAT of ₹106 crore (+44% YoY). FY26 inflows were ₹1,660 crore (+29% YoY). The order book reached a record ₹4,300 crore by August 2026, driven by the ₹2,205 crore HAL Uttam AESA contract signed in July 2026. Management is targeting 15% FY27 revenue growth to approximately ₹1,350 crore, with a 6-7x long-term revenue opportunity cited. Astra has announced a space arm demerger (timeline TBD).
